steps.title: The Driver Station
steps.say: This strip at the bottom is your **Driver Station**. It's how you build your code, run it in the simulator, and control the robot, just like the laptop at a real match.

steps.title: Before you build
steps.say: If the editor finds a mistake, it underlines it in red and counts it down here. Fix those first, because code with errors won't build.

steps.title: Start
steps.say: **Start** does two things: it **builds** your code (turns your Java into something the robot can run), then **runs** it in the simulator.

steps.title: Watch the status
steps.say: This shows where it's up to: **Building**, then **Running**. The first build takes the longest, and later ones are quicker.

steps.title: The console
steps.say: Everything your code prints with `System.out.println` shows up here. So do build errors: if the build fails, look here for the **file name and line number** it's unhappy about.

steps.title: Mode
steps.say: Pick what the robot should do: **Teleop** (you drive), **Auto** (it drives itself), or **Test**.

steps.title: Enable
steps.say: Robot code starts **disabled**, so nothing moves until you say so. Press **Enable** to let it run, and **Disable** to stop it at once. Same as a real robot.

steps.title: Change, then restart
steps.say: After you change your code, press **Restart**. It builds the new version and runs it. **Stop** ends the run.
